description: The base language model without temporal adaptation exhibits a heavy, systemic positional prior toward option (a) when prompted with unconstrained multiple-choice QA.

rotations.note: Correct purely by accidental alignment between positional bias and permutation slot.

scientific_interpretation.root_cause: Pre-trained autoregressive models have seen asymmetric token patterns in instruction/pre-training mixtures where the first enumerated item '(a)' has higher prior logit mass. Without fine-tuning or temporal steering, the model falls back to the default position prior rather than reasoning over question text.
scientific_interpretation.evaluation_implication: Evaluating an unadapted model on a single static slot distribution produces artificial variance depending on how many gold labels happen to occupy slot (a).

verdict.summary: Base Qwen2.5-3B exhibits an overwhelming preference for slot (a), yielding low canonical and strict accuracy (6.25%) when options rotate.
